|-- [M] Surface is the integration boundary (src/Surface.zig)
|   |-- Exposes init(), keyCallback(), mouseButtonCallback(), sizeCallback(), draw()
|   |   `-- Native UI events enter here; platform-independent terminal behavior stays here
|   |-- apprt.runtime.App / Surface supply the platform boundary (src/apprt.zig)
|   |   |-- Compile-time runtime selection: GTK, embedded, browser, or none
|   |   `-- rt_app.performAction() delegates titles, clipboard/UI actions, and window operations
|   `-- App connects multiple sessions (src/App.zig)
|       |-- surfaces: ArrayList(*apprt.Surface); focused_surface identifies the active session
|       |-- font_grid_set: font.SharedGridSet; device: ?*renderer.Device
|       |   `-- Surfaces reference shared fonts and borrow the app-scoped graphics device
|       `-- tick() -> drainMailbox() -> surfaceMessage() -> Surface.handleMessage()
|           `-- Worker-originated surface messages return to the application thread
|
|-- [O] Surface.init() assembles one session (src/Surface.zig)
|   |-- io: termio.Termio; io_thread: termio.Thread; io_thr: std.Thread
|   |-- renderer: Renderer; renderer_thread: renderer.Thread; renderer_thr: std.Thread
|   |-- renderer_state: renderer.State
|   |   |-- terminal = &self.io.terminal -- shared reference, not another terminal model
|   |   `-- mutex protects referenced terminal state and shared presentation inputs
|   |-- mouse / keyboard / pressed_key / focused / visible / readonly
|   |   `-- Interaction state belongs to the session, independently of the child process
|   `-- config: DerivedConfig; size: renderer.Size; font_grid_key
|       `-- Derived configuration avoids retaining the caller's Config memory
|
|-- [C] User input -> bindings or terminal bytes (src/Surface.zig)
|   |-- keyCallback() first resolves configured keybindings and sequences
|   |   |-- Handled bindings perform actions rather than sending the key to the child
|   |   `-- encodeKey() -> input.key_encode.encode() for unconsumed input
|   |       `-- [D] KeyEvent + Options.fromTerminal() -> protocol-specific bytes
|   |           `-- Terminal modes and active-screen keyboard settings affect encoding
|   |-- Mouse / selection / paste paths
|   |   |-- input.mouse_encode: event + terminal reporting mode -> mouse protocol bytes
|   |   |-- Screen.select() retains a tracked selection for local interaction
|   |   `-- input.paste.encode(): paste contents + options -> terminal input sequences
|   `-- queueIo(.write_small / .write_stable / .write_alloc)
|       |-- readonly rejects writes while retaining local terminal interactions
|       `-- Termio.queueMessage() -> termio.Thread.drainMailbox() -> queueWrite()
|           `-- Exec.queueWrite() schedules bytes to the PTY (src/termio/Exec.zig)
|
|-- [C] Child output -> parsed terminal operations (src/termio/Termio.zig)
|   |-- backend: termio.Backend = .exec; Exec owns Subprocess
|   |   |-- Surface supplies command, environment, working directory, shell integration
|   |   `-- Exec.threadEnter() -> Subprocess.start(): create PTY and launch command
|   |       |-- Process watcher detects child exit
|   |       `-- ReadThread delivers output to Termio.processOutput()
|   |           |-- POSIX: io-gather batches PTY reads; io-reader parses batches
|   |           `-- Windows: one read loop reads and processes output
|   |-- processOutput() locks renderer_state.mutex
|   |   `-- processOutputLocked() -> terminal_stream.nextSlice(buf)
|   |       |-- terminal.Stream(StreamHandler) retains incremental parsing state
|   |       `-- StreamHandler.vt() / vtPrintAscii() dispatch terminal operations
|   |           `-- print, cursor movement, scrolling, modes, and attributes mutate Terminal
|   `-- StreamHandler bridges effects outside the grid (src/termio/stream_handler.zig)
|       |-- Terminal queries -> termio_mailbox -> reply bytes to the child
|       |-- Titles, bells, clipboard requests -> surface_mailbox -> runtime handling
|       `-- queueRender() / renderer_mailbox -> renderer wakeup and presentation updates
|
|-- [O] Termio.terminal is the authoritative emulator model (src/terminal/Terminal.zig)
|   |-- Exposes print(), cursor operations, resize(), scrollViewport(), and mode changes
|   |   `-- Renderer-agnostic state: no native window or GPU ownership
|   |-- screens: ScreenSet (src/terminal/ScreenSet.zig)
|   |   |-- primary screen exists initially; alternate screen initializes on demand
|   |   `-- active: *Screen chooses the current screen
|   |       |-- cursor / saved_cursor / selection / charset / kitty_keyboard
|   |       |-- kitty_images and semantic_prompt retain screen-specific protocol state
|   |       `-- pages: PageList (src/terminal/Screen.zig, src/terminal/PageList.zig)
|   |           |-- Ordered pages hold scrollback followed by the active screen
|   |           |-- Page rows/cells carry character and styling data
|   |           `-- Tracked pins keep cursor, viewport, and selection references meaningful
|   `-- rows / cols / scrolling_region / tabstops / modes / colors / title / pwd
|       `-- [D] Parsed output changes both visible contents and future input interpretation
|
|-- [C] Shared terminal state -> GPU presentation (src/renderer/Thread.zig)
|   |-- Wakeup -> drainMailbox() -> renderCallback() -> Renderer.updateFrame()
|   |-- Renderer = GenericRenderer(GraphicsAPI) (src/renderer.zig)
|   |   `-- GraphicsAPI is selected at compile time: Metal or OpenGL
|   |-- updateFrame() snapshots under State.lockDemand() / unlockDemand()
|   |   |-- terminal_state: terminal.RenderState retains renderer-side extracted state
|   |   |-- [D] Viewport cells + dirty state + selection + cursor + images
|   |   |   `-- Combined with fonts, colors, sizing, mouse state, and IME preedit
|   |   `-- synchronized_output mode defers frame updates
|   |-- font_shaper / font_shaper_cache + font_grid -> glyph and cell rendering data
|   |   `-- src/renderer/generic.zig keeps frame construction separate from terminal parsing
|   `-- drawFrame() -> GraphicsAPI rendering and presentation
|       |-- Renderer scheduling considers visibility and vsync
|       `-- Surface.draw() can request synchronous drawing during native UI activity
|
|-- [D] Resize and configuration coordinate all session parts
|   |-- Surface.sizeCallback() -> resize() (src/Surface.zig)
|   |   |-- Pixel dimensions + cell metrics + padding -> renderer.Size.grid()
|   |   `-- queueIo(.resize) and renderer mailbox carry the new size
|   |       `-- Termio.resize() (src/termio/Termio.zig)
|   |           |-- Under the terminal mutex: backend.resize() + Terminal.resize()
|   |           |   `-- Child redraw cannot be parsed against obsolete dimensions
|   |           `-- Notify renderer after emulator and PTY size changes
|   `-- App.updateConfig() -> Surface.handleMessage(.change_config)
|       `-- Surface, Termio, and Renderer maintain their own derived configuration

`-- [O] Session teardown follows resource dependencies (src/Surface.zig)
    |-- close() -> rt_surface.close(needsConfirmQuit()) -> runtime-driven destruction
    |-- deinit(): stop optional search, then stop/join renderer and I/O threads

    |-- Only after workers stop: deinit renderer, thread managers, and Termio
    |   `-- Renderer is destroyed before its thread manager to retire display-link callbacks

   156	    /// Send a renderer message and unlock the renderer state mutex
   157	    /// if necessary to ensure we don't deadlock.
   158	    ///
   159	    /// This assumes the renderer state mutex is locked.
   160	    inline fn rendererMessageWriter(
   161	        self: *StreamHandler,
   162	        msg: renderer.Message,
   163	    ) void {
   164	        // See termio.Mailbox.send for more details on how this works.
   165	
   166	        // Try instant first. If it works then we can return.
   167	        if (self.renderer_mailbox.push(msg, .{ .instant = {} }) > 0) {
   168	            return;
   169	        }
   170	
   171	        // Instant would have blocked. Release the renderer mutex,
   172	        // wake up the renderer to allow it to process the message,
   173	        // and then try again.
   174	        self.renderer_state.mutex.unlock(global.io());
   175	        defer self.renderer_state.mutex.lockUncancelable(global.io());
   176	        self.renderer_wakeup.notify() catch |err| {
   177	            // This is an EXTREMELY unlikely case. We still don't return
   178	            // and attempt to send the message because its most likely
   179	            // that everything is fine, but log in case a freeze happens.
   180	            log.warn(
   181	                "failed to notify renderer, may deadlock err={}",
   182	                .{err},
   183	            );
   184	        };
   185	        _ = self.renderer_mailbox.push(msg, .{ .forever = {} });
   186	    }

   208	    inline fn vtFallible(
   209	        self: *StreamHandler,
   210	        comptime action: Stream.Action.Tag,
   211	        value: Stream.Action.Value(action),
   212	    ) !void {
   213	        // The branch hints here are based on real world data
   214	        // which indicates that the most common actions are:
   215	        //
   216	        // 1. print
   217	        // 2. set_attributes
   218	        // 3. carriage_return
   219	        // 4. line_feed
   220	        // 5. cursor_pos
   221	        //
   222	        // Together, these 5 actions make up nearly 98% of
   223	        // all actions encountered in real world scenarios.
   224	        //
   225	        // ref: https://github.com/qwerasd205/asciinema-stats
   226	        switch (action) {
   227	            .print => {
   228	                @branchHint(.likely);
   229	                try self.terminal.print(value.cp);
   230	            },
   231	            .print_slice => {
   232	                @branchHint(.likely);
   233	                try self.terminal.printSlice(value.cps);
   234	            },
   235	            .print_repeat => try self.terminal.printRepeat(value),
   236	            .bell => self.bell(),
   237	            .backspace => self.terminal.backspace(),
   238	            .horizontal_tab => self.horizontalTab(value),
   239	            .horizontal_tab_back => self.horizontalTabBack(value),
   240	            .linefeed => {
   241	                @branchHint(.likely);
   242	                try self.linefeed();
   243	            },
   244	            .carriage_return => {
   245	                @branchHint(.likely);
   246	                self.terminal.carriageReturn();
   247	            },
   248	            .enquiry => try self.enquiry(),
   249	            .invoke_charset => self.terminal.invokeCharset(value.bank, value.charset, value.locking),
   250	            .cursor_up => self.terminal.cursorUp(value.value),
   251	            .cursor_down => self.terminal.cursorDown(value.value),
   252	            .cursor_left => self.terminal.cursorLeft(value.value),
   253	            .cursor_right => self.terminal.cursorRight(value.value),
   254	            .cursor_pos => {
   255	                @branchHint(.likely);

   511	    start: std.Io.Timestamp,
   512	    exited: bool = false,
   513	
   514	    /// The data stream is the main IO for the pty.
   515	    write_stream: xev.Stream,
   516	
   517	    /// The process watcher
   518	    process: ?xev.Process,
   519	
   520	    /// This is the pool of available (unused) write states. If you grab
   521	    /// one from the pool, you must put it back when you're done!
   522	    write_pool: std.heap.MemoryPool(Write) = .empty,
   523	
   524	    /// The write queue for the data stream.

   526	
   527	    /// This is used for both waiting for the process to exit and then
   528	    /// subsequently to wait for the data_stream to close.

   530	
   531	    // The completion specific to Flatpak process waiting. If
   532	    // we aren't compiling with Flatpak support this is zero-sized.
   533	    flatpak_wait_c: FlatpakHostCommand.Completion = .{},

   536	    read_thread: std.Thread,
   537	    read_thread_pipe: posix.fd_t,
   538	    read_thread_fd: posix.fd_t,
   539	
   540	    /// The timer to detect termios state changes.
   541	    termios_timer: xev.Timer,
   542	    termios_timer_c: xev.Completion = .{},
   543	    termios_timer_running: bool = true,
   544	
   545	    /// The last known termios mode. Used for change detection
   546	    /// to prevent unnecessary locking of expensive mutexes.
   547	    termios_mode: ptypkg.Mode = .{},
   548	
   549	    pub fn deinit(self: *ThreadData, alloc: Allocator) void {
   550	        _ = posix.system.close(self.read_thread_pipe);
   551	
   552	        // Clear our write pool. We know we aren't ever going to do
   553	        // any more IO since we stop our data stream below so we can just
   554	        // drop this.
   555	        self.write_pool.deinit(alloc);

   557	        // Stop our process watcher
   558	        if (self.process) |*p| p.deinit();

   560	        // Stop our write stream
   561	        self.write_stream.deinit();

   563	        // Stop our termios timer
   564	        self.termios_timer.deinit();
   565	    }

  1269	/// The read thread works with a companion gather thread to form a two-stage
  1270	/// pipeline that moves pty output into the terminal:
  1271	///
  1272	///   io-gather:  read()/poll() the pty into one of a few rotating
  1273	///               buffers, batching bulk output.
  1274	///   io-reader:  hand each filled buffer to processOutput (terminal
  1275	///               lock, VT parse, state update, render scheduling).
  1276	///
  1277	/// This used to be a single serial loop (and still is on Windows):
  1278	///
  1279	///   while (true) { blocking_read(); exit_if_eof(); process(); }
  1280	///
  1281	/// I found on macOS that the kernel tty output queue caps every read
  1282	/// on the master at 1 KB no matter how large the read buffer is. This means
  1283	/// that producers (e.g. `cat`) stall with the above architecture because
  1284	/// there are windows in the `process()` part where we aren't draining
  1285	/// the kernel pty fd.
  1286	///
  1287	/// Instead, having a separate thread gather and drain the kernel pty
  1288	/// into a rotating set of preallocated buffers minimizes this stall
  1289	/// period to effectively zero: while the io-reader thread parses
  1290	/// one batch, the gather thread is draining the kernel queue. There is
  1291	/// still stalling (our VT parse is a bottleneck now), but we don't stall
  1292	/// between them.
  1293	///
  1294	/// Interactive latency is preserved: a batch is delivered on the
  1295	/// first EAGAIN unless the stream is saturated (>= 1 KiB gathered
  1296	/// means the writer filled the kernel queue), in which case we bridge
  1297	/// the producer's microsecond refill gaps with a short poll, bounded
  1298	/// by a small total budget per batch that is well under a display
  1299	/// frame. This means that small outputs that are more typical continue
  1300	/// to be interactive.
  1301	///
  1302	/// We use basic poll/read syscalls here because we are only
  1303	/// monitoring two fds and this is still much faster and lower
  1304	/// overhead than any async mechanism.
  1305	pub const ReadThread = struct {
  1306	    /// The number of buffers rotated between the gather and parse
  1307	    /// stages. The gather stage can run at most this many batches
  1308	    /// ahead of the parse stage before it blocks, which (via the
  1309	    /// kernel pty queue) is also what preserves flow control to the
  1310	    /// child. Empirically chosen through measurements on an M4 Max.
  1311	    /// Less than 4 there are minor slowdowns, above 4 there are no
  1312	    /// improvements.
  1313	    const buffer_count = 4;
  1314	
  1315	    /// The capacity of each gather buffer. One batch is also the unit
  1316	    /// of work the parse stage does per terminal lock acquisition, so
  1317	    /// this bounds both gather latency and lock hold time.
  1318	    const buffer_capacity = 64 * 1024;
  1319	
  1320	    /// How many gathered bytes mark a stream as saturated. The macOS
  1321	    /// kernel tty output queue hands the master at most about 1 KiB
  1322	    /// per read, so gathering a full 1 KiB means the writer filled
  1323	    /// the queue (a bulk stream worth briefly waiting on), while
  1324	    /// anything smaller is an interactive trickle that must be
  1325	    /// delivered with no added latency.
  1326	    const bridge_threshold = 1024;
  1327	
  1328	    /// How many times an EAGAIN on a saturated stream is retried
  1329	    /// with an immediate read before we're willing to sleep in poll.
  1330	    /// Basically, a spin retry.
  1331	    ///
  1332	    /// The writer refills the drained kernel queue within a few
  1333	    /// microseconds, while a sleep and wakeup through poll costs
  1334	    /// several more. If the gather stage sleeps on every refill gap,
  1335	    /// the whole pipeline degenerates to lockstep with the writer at
  1336	    /// about 1 KiB per wakeup. A short burst of nonblocking reads
  1337	    /// bridges nearly all refill gaps without sleeping. Measured, 8
  1338	    /// to 16 retries catches over 90% of the gaps and nearly doubles
  1339	    /// the saturated drain rate, and larger values helped little.
  1340	    /// The cost is bounded to at most this many extra ~0.5us read
  1341	    /// syscalls per gap, and we only spin on streams that already
  1342	    /// gathered a full kernel queue, so an idle or interactive
  1343	    /// terminal never spins.
  1344	    const bridge_spin_max = 16;

  1401	        idle_write_fd: posix.fd_t = -1,
  1402	
  1403	        /// Set by the gather stage when the stream is over (quit

  1405	        /// remaining batches and then exits.
  1406	        done: bool = false,
  1407	
  1408	        /// The buffer storage itself.
  1409	        bufs: [buffer_count][buffer_capacity]u8 = undefined,
  1410	    };

  1412	    fn threadMainPosix(fd: posix.fd_t, io: *termio.Termio, quit: posix.fd_t) void {

  1522	    /// The gather stage. This drains the pty into rotating buffers,
